search.query: index=`riskability_index_findings` sourcetype=riskability:findings record_type="match_receipt" earliest=0 latest=+10y _index_earliest=`riskability_stuck_window` _index_latest=now | stats max(match_run) AS match_run, sum(findings_produced) AS findings_produced BY hostname | where findings_produced > 0 | lookup riskability_matchstate_lookup hostname OUTPUT folded_run | eval acknowledged = if(isnotnull(folded_run) AND abs(tonumber(folded_run) - match_run) < 300, 1, 0) | where acknowledged == 0 | stats count AS stale

dashboard.label: Fleet overview
dashboard.description: Vulnerability posture across every host reporting a swinv inventory.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_feedstate_lookup | where isnotnull(imported_at) | eval age_days = round((now() - imported_at)/86400, 1) | fields age_days
index=`riskability_index_inventory` sourcetype=riskability:swinv earliest=-7d | stats dc(hostname) AS hosts
| inputlookup riskability_hostecostate_lookup | where hostname="__fleet__" | stats sum(instances) AS components

div.b: Some hosts have been matched but their results have not been folded in.
div.span: The open counts on this page are stale-high for those hosts, and closing is being withheld for them until the fold completes. Nothing here is under-reporting risk; it may be over-reporting it. The hosts are listed below. This normally clears by itself within the hour; if it does not, the pipeline has stopped and Admin shows which job.

search.query: index=`riskability_index_findings` sourcetype=riskability:findings record_type="match_receipt" earliest=0 latest=+10y _index_earliest=`riskability_stuck_window` _index_latest=now | stats max(match_run) AS match_run, sum(findings_produced) AS findings_produced BY hostname | where findings_produced > 0 | lookup riskability_matchstate_lookup hostname OUTPUT folded_run | eval acknowledged = if(isnotnull(folded_run) AND abs(tonumber(folded_run) - match_run) < 300, 1, 0) | where acknowledged == 0 | eval matched = strftime(match_run, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | eval folded = if(isnull(folded_run) OR folded_run="", "never", strftime(tonumber(folded_run), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")) | eval waiting = tostring(round(now() - match_run), "duration") | table hostname, matched, findings_produced, folded, waiting | rename hostname AS "Host", matched AS "Matched at", findings_produced AS "Findings the matcher reported", folded AS "Last folded in", waiting AS "Waiting"
| `riskability_accepted_findings` | where isnotnull(kev_added) AND kev_added!="" | stats dc(cve_id) AS n

single.option: on the CISA KEV list, and excepted

div.b: Accepted risks are excluded from every other number on this page.
div.span: An accepted risk is one somebody has looked at and decided to handle another way, recorded with what that other way is. It is still a vulnerability, and it is still present. A fleet showing no open findings and four hundred accepted ones is not a clean fleet, which is why the count sits here rather than being hidden. Manage them on Risk exceptions.

panel.title: Where the open findings are, by package

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_openstate_dim_lookup | where dim="package" | rename value AS package | table package, cves | sort 50000 - cves | head 60

viz.option: No open findings. If no feed has been imported this means the app cannot assess anything yet, not that the fleet is clean — check the Feed administration page.

html.div:
Click a tile to see the findings behind that package. Area is distinct CVEs, not severity.
A large tile is a package carrying many open CVEs, so it is where patching effort goes furthest. That is not the same as where the single worst vulnerability is — for that, sort the Findings page by EPSS.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_openstate_dim_lookup | where dim="confidence" | rename value AS confidence | eval sev = confidence | sort 50000 confidence | fields confidence, sev, findings

viz.option: Nothing matched. With no feed imported the matcher has nothing to compare against.

div.span: High means the package identity and version were both read from a package record. Low means the identity was inferred — every Windows finding lands here. Informational means the version could not be compared properly. Only the high band should drive patching decisions.

search.query: | `riskability_open_findings` | where confidence!="informational" | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves, dc(package) AS packages BY hostname | sort 50000 - cves | head 20

viz.option: No host has an open finding. If no inventory has arrived, that is silence rather than a clean fleet.

panel.title: Known-exploited vulnerabilities present in the fleet (CISA KEV)

div.b: These are being exploited in the wild right now.
div.span: CISA lists them as known-exploited, which is a stronger signal than any severity score: it is not a prediction. Click a row to see every finding for that CVE. Where several advisories describe the same CVE, the shortest description is shown: a distribution's one-line summary says what the flaw is, where NVD's runs to a paragraph about affected versions.

search.query: | `riskability_open_findings` | where confidence!="informational" | where isnotnull(kev_added) AND kev_added!="" | eval tlen = len(title) | eventstats min(tlen) AS shortest BY cve_id | eval short_title = if(tlen == shortest, title, null()) | stats dc(hostname) AS hosts, values(package) AS packages, values(kev_added) AS kev_added, values(kev_due) AS kev_due, max(epss) AS epss, values(short_title) AS title BY cve_id | eval title = mvindex(title, 0) | eval epss_pct = if(isnotnull(epss), round(epss * 100, 1), null()) | sort 50000 - hosts | table cve_id, title, hosts, packages, kev_added, kev_due, epss_pct | rename cve_id AS "CVE", title AS "What it is", hosts AS "Hosts", packages AS "Packages", kev_added AS "Added to KEV", kev_due AS "Remediate by", epss_pct AS "EPSS %"

viz.option: No known-exploited CVEs matched. This panel is only as good as the KEV catalogue in the imported bundle — if KEV was unreachable when the bundle was built, it is blank for that reason.
